title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
pattern: Tree recursion: best single branch vs best bending path
statement: A **path** is any chain of connected nodes in a binary tree (it need not pass through the root, and it may not visit a node twice). Return the largest possible sum of the values along a path.

example.why: The best path is 15 → 20 → 7, with sum 42. Going up through −10 would only lower it.

idea: Every path has one highest node where it *bends*: it may come up one branch, pass through the node, and go down the other branch.
For each node compute the best sum of a **single branch** going downward from it. A branch with a negative sum is simply not taken (count it as 0).
At each node, `left branch + node + right branch` is the best path bending there — compare it with the best so far. But to its parent a node can offer only **one** branch, because a path cannot fork.

complexity.spaceWhy: The recursion stack is as deep as the tree's height h.

steps.text: Our example: **`root = [-10,9,20,None,None,15,7]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`self.max_sum` keeps the best path found so far. The small labels that will appear beside nodes are the best **single branch** each node can offer its parent.
At node 9: the best branch down-left is worth 0 and down-right 0 (a negative branch is dropped, counting as 0). The path bending here sums to 0 + 9 + 0 = **9**. Best so far: **9**.
A path cannot fork, so node 9 offers its parent only its better branch: max(0, 0) + 9 = **9**.
At node 15: the best branch down-left is worth 0 and down-right 0 (a negative branch is dropped, counting as 0). The path bending here sums to 0 + 15 + 0 = **15**. Best so far: **15**.
A path cannot fork, so node 15 offers its parent only its better branch: max(0, 0) + 15 = **15**.
At node 7: the best branch down-left is worth 0 and down-right 0 (a negative branch is dropped, counting as 0). The path bending here sums to 0 + 7 + 0 = **7**. Best so far: **15**.
A path cannot fork, so node 7 offers its parent only its better branch: max(0, 0) + 7 = **7**.
At node 20: the best branch down-left is worth 15 and down-right 7 (a negative branch is dropped, counting as 0). The path bending here sums to 15 + 20 + 7 = **42**. Best so far: **42**.
A path cannot fork, so node 20 offers its parent only its better branch: max(15, 7) + 20 = **35**.
At node -10: the best branch down-left is worth 9 and down-right 35 (a negative branch is dropped, counting as 0). The path bending here sums to 9 + -10 + 35 = **34**. Best so far: **42**.
A path cannot fork, so node -10 offers its parent only its better branch: max(9, 35) + -10 = **25**.
The best path anywhere in the tree sums to **42**.
Done — the answer is **`42`**. The best path is 15 → 20 → 7, with sum 42. Going up through −10 would only lower it.
